summary: Only the door-3 bar's upper face changed (7d07806 candidate; the ink print is the w21 version after the f9956d5 revert, so the baseline is w21 B 8.8). The bar now has the same layout as the in-service face in omaat_j32: a control panel over two light-grey ovens with blue LED readouts, a landscape monitor on a ledge over two open bays (brewer with a green LED on the left, water bottles on the right as in knav_31), a tall glass-door cabinet with a round latch, a caution plate and a cream 'return to seat' tag, a near-black counter, the blind rolled away and no tumblers or bottle shelf. Measured against j32: oven doors L132 (photo L136), glass interior L49 (L57), q11 carcass frame L56 (integration target 50-70), m05 counter L26 (j32 L39). Side by side (scratchpad/raterMonoB/pair.jpg: j32 | m06 | q11) there is no structural mismatch left, so this is now clearly the same product. What remains is finish and detail, all low: the glass cabinet reads like an open shelved display, not dark tinted glass; the nosing is a flat white band, not a rounded satin-aluminium rail; the counter shows no mirror reflections; the oven fronts are simplified; the right open bay is crushed to black. q01, q13 and q19 are pixel-identical, so their scores carry over. The door-2 welcome galley shares serviceFace and is reported pixel-identical.
lighting_note: Not scored here. The lower ash doors render L172-184 (q11, m06) against L134-149 in j32; that photo's cabin light is dimmer and warmer, so this is mostly exposure (grain SD 5 vs 4-5 matches). j32's counter mirrors the ovens and monitor, but the env model has no local reflections. The right open bay renders L3 in m05 against L12 in j32, so the shadow or AO in the bay is crushed.

Target L50-70 met. Counter: q11 (130-560,345-380) mean L77 -> L68 (the grazing view picks up an env sheen); in the frontal m05 (150-700,440-480) it reads L26, against j32's counter (300-640,640-760) L39 with p10 10 / p90 77. The integration asked for a 15 mm satin-steel nosing (#9a9ea3); that part was not done (see the low issue).

calibration.issue: Location evidence: is omaat_j32 the door-3 bar?
calibration.evidence: Three independent sources agree. OMAAT's text puts the bar between the middle and rear business cabins, and in the 64-seat THE Room layout door 3 is the only cross-aisle that splits J, with the bar as its only self-service monument. trafficnews 2019 shows the same carcass: black upper unit, monitor at the top right of the face, glass-lit strip to its right, a near-black counter wrapping round, pale lower doors with an aluminium nosing, and J seating behind the curtain. knav_31 shows the same monitor over open bays with bottles, the glass door with round latch and 'return to seat' plate, and a lav door with a lav sign immediately to the right, which matches q11's lav at the right. The 2019 press render plus trafficnews show the factory fit with the blind down. omaat_j32 (2020) and knav show the in-service face with the blind up, so following the in-service face is the right call. The one caveat is that the blind exists, and the model now hides it entirely in a black head. That matches j32.

issues.title: The glass-door cabinet reads as an open shelved display, not a dark tinted glass door
issues.evidence: q11 cabinet (425-555,145-375) and m05 (640-800,100-410): light shelf rails and box outlines (L~110-140) are clearly legible through the glass, and the door frame is a thin light-grey rim. In j32 (700-950,130-760) the glass is dark smoked (interior L57, p90 83), the contents are only faint, and a wide near-black door stile (~8 % of the door width, L23) carries the oval latch boss. The mean values match (L49 vs L57); the problem is the structure.
issues.fix: 10_mono.js serviceFace, cabinet: lower the glass transmission or tint it darker (#2a2826 at about 0.45), drop the contents/shelf colour to L<=70 (#4a4744), and widen the door stile to 0.035 m in the carcass colour #3a3835 with the latch on a raised 0.06 x 0.09 m oval boss. Check that the door-2 galley wants the same, since it shares the helper.

issues.title: The counter nosing is a flat bright-white band; in service it is a rounded satin-aluminium rail
issues.evidence: m05 (100-700,500-512) L220 uniform, s0.02. In j32 (raterMonoB/j32_lower.png) the rail is ~25 mm, round-topped, with a highlight line ~L180-200 over a mid-grey body ~L110-140 and a dark shadow line under it. trafficnews also shows a grey-silver rail, not white.
issues.fix: 10_mono.js MONMAT.nosing: '#e4e5e6' r0.3 m0.25 -> '#b8babc' r0.28 m0.7, and in buildBar make the front piece a 0.025 m half-round (gCyl, radius 0.0125) or a gRBoxM with r=0.010, so it gets a highlight and a shadow line.

issues.title: Simplified oven fronts
issues.evidence: m05 ovens (180-305,235-390): flat panel, cream square tag and a straight bar handle. j32 (175-330,320-600): each door has a large round recessed dish with a vertical lever across it, a black grille/readout strip across the top with the blue LED at its left end, and blue paper tags.
issues.fix: serviceFace ovens: add a 0.10 m diameter dark-grey ring (gCyl, 0.006 deep, #8c8f92) behind the handle at mid-height, and recolour the tag to pale blue #9fc3dc.

issues.title: Carried: canopy and cheeks over the bar
issues.evidence: j32 and trafficnews show pale lit ceiling panels directly over the unit (trafficnews top band L~230), with no ash cheeks beside the upper carcass: j32 has a lit grey side face and a white wall to the right.
